column1: # Game profile of 30XX (Switch, update 1.3.6 = v851968). On the Mac through the title into the first level with scripted input; the iPhone is not tested yet
# Batterystaple Games' own engine, SDK 13.3.5, sound through FMOD. It renders with NVIDIA's desktop OpenGL 4.5 through EGL: it binds OpenGL ES first only to list the EGL
# configurations, then makes a desktop 4.5 context and fills its buffers by name (direct state access). main gets its GL functions from a glad loader (eglGetProcAddress), which the
# host's GL layer implements on Metal (dm/gfx/gl/hle_gl.m). The shaders are #version 120 GLSL the engine puts together at run time from one shared header and a body: no game
# file holds them whole, so the NSP script captures them by booting the game on the Mac (gl_capture.tsv lists them) and dm/gfx/tools/gl_shaders.py translates them offline

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# The game ships no sdk module: Nintendo's SDK is subsdk0 (its nnSdk-13_3_5 string and StandardAllocator), which the host searches as the SDK (dm_sdk_modules). subsdk1 / subsdk2
# are NVIDIA's OpenGL driver and GLSLC, which program the GPU through NvRm: never loaded, the GL layer answers main's EGL imports
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so the game has no virtual address memory (IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon): main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB,
# a 3328 MB heap region. About 2.5 GB resident on the Mac in the first level (1.8 GB of it Metal allocations)
# no NVN shaders: the NVN tables stay empty (gl_shaders.py writes the GL library and its table, not the profile)

column2: 30XX has no NVN shaders (its GLSL shaders go through the GL layer)
